title: Stored photometry for a past session is invisible: the light curve is filtered by the CURRENT global target selection, so reviewing any other night shows "has no data yet"
summary: Closed by an earlier wave and verified by me at the cause, not the symptom. science_analytics_tab.dart:307-313 resolves the object id from the SESSION'S OWN rows before keying sessionLightCurveProvider (helper: science_analytics_tab/navigation_and_snapshots.dart:320-349), and only promotes rows with role=='target' and a non-null differentialMagnitude, so a comparison star is never redrawn as the target's curve. I checked the fix reaches all three reported symptoms rather than just the chart: the resolved id feeds lightCurvePoints for the ladder (science_analytics_tab.dart:539 and :587), the AAVSO export button's visibility gate (:753) and PeriodAnalysisPanel (:776), and the campaign strip (:387). I also checked the export was not merely re-enabled over the wrong data - AavsoExportService partitions the session's own rows by role (aavso_export_service.dart:82-113) and never reads the live selection, so it exports that night's target. No relocation.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_reviewed_light_curve_test.dart - 2 cases against the real ScienceAnalyticsTab widget: stored rows on 'V-TEST' with an empty live selection (global fallback 'target_primary') still plot, and a session holding only role=='comparison' rows draws nothing.
revert_check: Deleted the `photometryObjectId = _reviewedPhotometryObjectId(rows: ..., liveSelection: photometryObjectId);` assignment at science_analytics_tab.dart:307-310 so the provider is keyed on the live selection again. Test failed: 'Found 0 widgets with text "Differential Photometry"' (1 of 2). Restored -> 2/2 pass.

title: Science guide ladder is stuck on rung 1 and tells the user to "turn on live photometry" while the same page plots an 80-point light curve, a period and an Export to AAVSO button
summary: Closed by an earlier wave at the cause. evaluateLadder (science_ladder_model.dart:104-131) no longer cascades: measure is never locked, track is done when lightCurvePoints > 0 (points are proof the star was tracked), curve keys off the point count, period off hasPeriodResult / >=10 points, contribute off hasExportableData. The locked-reason strings the finding quoted are in science_ladder_card.dart:_prerequisiteFor (:177-192) - the finding's location_wrong correction is right, they are not in science_rung_sheet.dart - and they now return null for the two rungs that can never lock, so the sheet (science_rung_sheet.dart:57, which renders the padlock only for RungState.locked) cannot state a prerequisite the user has already met. Going deep on this one turned up the same rung lying in the OPPOSITE direction; fixed separately below.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_ladder_evidence_test.dart - 3 cases driving the real ScienceLadderCard (taps the rung chips, reads the real sheets) with hasCalibration:false, lightCurvePoints:80, hasPeriodResult:true.
revert_check: Restored the cascade at science_ladder_model.dart:109-120 (track = locked whenever measure != done, else done only when photometryLive && hasTarget; curve = locked whenever track != done). Two tests failed: 'the light-curve rung is not padlocked over an 80-point curve' (found the 'start collecting points' padlock) and 'evidence beats the cascade' (Expected RungState.done, Actual RungState.locked). Restored -> 3/3 pass.

title: Exported MPC 80-column report puts the CCD observation-type code in column 14 instead of column 15, so every record is malformed
summary: Closed by an earlier wave. mpc_export_service.dart:183 writes note1 = ' ' (column 14, the program/publication note) and :188 writes note2 = 'C' (column 15, the observation type), assembled at :228; the header comment at :157-158 was corrected too. I re-derived the column map against the MPC optical-observation format instead of trusting the comment: 1-5 number, 6-12 designation, 13 discovery asterisk, 14 Note 1, 15 Note 2, 16-32 date, 33-44 RA, 45-56 Dec, 57-65 blank, 66-70 F5.2 magnitude, 71 band, 72-77 blank, 78-80 observatory code - which is what the code emits, and the 80-column length check at :232 still passes.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/science/mpc_export_column_layout_test.dart - 3 cases through the real MpcExportService.generateReport: the type code at index 14, index 13 blank, the surrounding fixed-width fields undisturbed, and an astrometry-only row. That is the production entry point for both buttons - mpc_export_panel.dart:319 (Copy) calls it directly and mpc_export_panel.dart:289 -> mpc_export_service.dart:125 (Export to File) calls it too.
revert_check: Swapped the two constants back (note1 = 'C', note2 = ' ') at mpc_export_service.dart:183/188. Two of three tests failed: "Expected: ' ' / Actual: 'C'" on the column-14 assertion. Restored -> 3/3 pass.

title: Photometry CSV export writes local wall-clock timestamps with no timezone, silently shifting every measurement by the observer's UTC offset
summary: Closed by an earlier wave across the whole surface, not just the dataset that was reported. science_export_hub.dart:111 defines _utcStamp(dt) => dt.toUtc().toIso8601String(); I audited every timestamp the file emits rather than trusting that: all seven dataset writers call it (:1129, :1183, :1244, :1292, :1342, :1394, :1450), all seven headers read 'Timestamp (UTC)' (:1098, :1145, :1217, :1266, :1313, :1365, :1418), the photometry CSV gained a JD column (_julianDate at :116, header at :1099), and both filename stamps (:925-928 CSV, :1013-1016 report) are .toUtc() with an explicit 'Z' suffix. No raw local toIso8601String() remains in the file.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_export_hub_truth_test.dart - 'photometry CSV timestamps are UTC and carry a JD column' drives the real ScienceExportHub, taps the real CSV button and captures what the production writer provider is handed, asserting '2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z' and JD 2461253.875 for a row stored at 09:00 UTC.
revert_check: Changed _utcStamp to `dt.toIso8601String()` (dropping .toUtc()) and ran under TZ=America/New_York, the timezone the finding was reproduced in. Test failed: Expected contains '2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z', actual CSV carried the 05:00 local stamp. Restored -> 2/2 pass. (The assertion is TZ-independent: on a UTC host the revert still drops the 'Z'.)

title: Transient Discovery Report: the AAVSO and MPC network chips are inert and the app never shows why, because the reason is only rendered for the already-selected network
summary: Closed by an earlier wave. transient_report_panel.dart:153-171 renders _disabledNotices(...) - one line for EVERY unavailable network - instead of the old single-format guard, and _disabledNotices (:394-409) collapses to ONE line when the blocker is the detection itself (unreviewed, or a dipole artefact) so the panel does not say the same thing three times. The chips also pass `enabled: enabled` (:139) rather than only a null onTap, so an unavailable network reads as unavailable instead of merely unpicked. The per-network reason strings at :411+ are now reachable without any interaction.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_reasons_test.dart - 2 cases against the real TransientReportPanel with a confirmed newSource detection and no credentials: every chip is onTap-null AND enabled:false, and all three reasons are on screen with no interaction; plus an unreviewed detection stating its one shared blocker once.
revert_check: Replaced the _disabledNotices(...) call at transient_report_panel.dart:154 with the old single-format guard ('_formatEnabled(_format, ...) ? [] : [_disabledReason(_format, ...)]'). Test failed: 'Found 0 widgets with text containing MPC astrometry is for moving objects'. Restored -> 2/2 pass.

title: Campaign Rollup contradicts itself three ways on one card: "Total integration 0.0h" beside "0.17h integration", and "No frames captured for this target yet" beside a session with 2 frames
summary: The earlier wave fixed the empty-state half and then re-created the same collision in the populated half. It relabelled the header tiles ('Integration (accepted)' / '(captured)', 'Mean HFR (session avg)'), the per-filter EMPTY state and the session rows - which now say 'Nh captured', meaning every frame the session took. But the two widgets that only render when there IS data still used the word 'captured' for the ACCEPTED subset: _OverallProgress printed 'Captured 0.0h of 5.0h goal' from rollup.totalCapturedIntegrationSecs, and _FilterRow printed 'N frames captured (no goal)' from CampaignFilterRollup.capturedFrames. Both are accepted-only by definition - campaign_rollup_service.dart:75-76 builds lightFrames as `frameType == 'light' && i.isAccepted`, and campaign_rollup.dart:16/19 documents the fields as accepted-only. So on a campaign with rejected frames the same card would read 'Captured 2.3h of ...' above '3.33h captured'. I renamed both to the population they actually count: campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:468 'Accepted Xh of Yh goal', :517 'N/M frames accepted', :528 'N frames accepted (no goal)'. Labels only - no number moved, so nothing downstream changes.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/campaign_rollup_populations_test.dart - new case 'the per-filter table and the goal bar name the same population', built on a new _partlyRejectedRollup() fixture (40 frames taken, 20 accepted, an L filter with a 50-frame goal and an R filter without one) because every existing case used `filters: const []` and no goal, so neither _FilterRow nor _OverallProgress was ever rendered. Asserts no 'frames captured' text survives, '20/50 frames accepted' and '8 frames accepted (no goal)' render, the goal bar says 'Accepted 2.3h of' and not 'Captured 2.3h of', and the session row still says '3.33h captured'.
revert_check: Restored the three original strings ('Captured ${...}h of ...', '${...}/${...} frames', '${...} frames captured (no goal)'). The new test failed: "Expected: no matching candidates / Actual: Found 1 widget with text containing frames captured". The four pre-existing cases still passed, which is why the residual survived the earlier wave. Restored -> 5/5 pass.
caveats: The finding's severity was corrected DOWN to P2 by the verifier and I agree: each number is individually defensible, nothing downstream consumes them.

title: Extra (found while going deep on the ladder): a period search stays on screen after the reviewed session changes, so the Science guide marks 'Analyse the period' done for a night that was never searched
summary: periodAnalysisProvider (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/period_analysis_provider.dart:193) is ONE global NotifierProvider with no session key, and nothing dropped it when the operator changed the session under review. So the Period Analysis card kept rendering the previous night's Lomb-Scargle/BLS result, and hasPeriodResult (science_analytics_tab.dart:465) kept feeding evaluateLadder - which, now that the cascade is gone, reports the period rung `done` on the strength of that stale value. That is the same guide-vs-page contradiction the finding above is about, running the other way, and it was reachable the moment the ladder stopped cascading. Fixed at the two production controls that change the reviewed session, matching the clearing the same handlers already do for _selectedFrameImageId ('The frame picked in the old session means nothing here'): the session dropdown's onChanged (science_analytics_tab.dart:177-189) and the 'Most recent' reset button (:211-217) now call periodAnalysisProvider.notifier.clear() before setState. This also stops the science report exporter (science_analytics_tab/navigation_and_snapshots.dart:172 reads the same result) from stamping one night's period into another night's report.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_period_result_session_scope_test.dart - drives the real ScienceAnalyticsTab with periodAnalysisProvider seeded with a GENUINE PeriodAnalysisResult (produced by the real PeriodAnalysisService over a 0.5 d sinusoid, so nothing is hand-built), taps the real DropdownButton<int> session picker, selects the other night, and reads periodAnalysisProvider.result from the live container.
revert_check: Deleted the `ref.read(periodAnalysisProvider.notifier).clear();` line from the dropdown's onChanged (science_analytics_tab.dart:183). Test failed: 'Expected: null / Actual: <Instance of PeriodAnalysisResult>'. Restored -> 1/1 pass.
caveats: Only the two user-driven session-change paths are cleared. A session change that happens without the picker (a live session starting mid-review) still carries the old result; that path needs the result to be session-keyed in the notifier, which is a larger change than this finding warrants.
